title: Symmetry reduction does not by itself discretize a spectrum
claim: The Lie-symmetry-preserving quantization fixes temporal exponents but leaves arbitrary functions of the reduced coordinate, while the difference-operator Hamiltonian lacks a common domain establishing its boundary condition, adjoint, completeness, and self-adjointness. Together they isolate the same concrete obstruction: local symmetry reduction can organize an evolution equation without supplying the global data that turn a continuum of amplitudes or formal states into a legitimate discrete spectrum.
historical_or_program_relation: The Lie-Noether route and the non-Hermitian Hilbert-Polya route begin from different dynamics, but both move the decisive burden from a formal differential expression to admissible boundary/domain data.
limits: The Lie-Noether unit does not rule out added boundary or global conditions and is not a no-go theorem for other quantizations. The difference-operator correspondence remains formal. Their shared obstruction neither identifies a common operator nor proves anything about the location of zeta zeros.

title: A scalar zeta kernel is not yet a spectral operator
claim: Residue-kernel design converts the alternating zeta series into a hyperbolic integral by choosing residues and a summable dependence on the discrete index; Fourier functional calculus converts a scalar function F into a translation-invariant operator by multiplying each momentum mode by F(k squared). These are successive but logically separate kinds of construction: an integral representation can control the scalar symbol, whereas an operator realization additionally needs a function space, convergence, geometry, and domain.
historical_or_program_relation: The integral-representation program supplies analytic control of zeta in a strip, while the zeta-field program promotes a completed critical-line function to a flat-space Fourier multiplier; juxtaposition exposes the missing operator-theoretic step rather than treating the shared zeta notation as a bridge.
limits: Neither source composes the two constructions. The integral has a stated strip and pole caveat and provides no spectrum. The Fourier definition assumes flat translation symmetry and suitable decay; its use in a physical Lagrangian is not a zeta spectral theorem and does not imply RH.

title: Trace weights must be produced by localization geometry
claim: In the hyperbolic calculation, diagonalizing a conjugacy representative and integrating over its centralizer strip leaves primitive length and repetition with a hyperbolic-sine weight; in the flow calculation, restricting the graph kernel to the diagonal and pushing it to time produces the primitive period divided by the determinant of one minus the Poincare return map. Both show that orbit coefficients are Jacobians of a localization procedure, not labels inserted after matching a spectral sequence.
historical_or_program_relation: The Selberg derivation is a concrete exact model for the later distributional fixed-point formulation: kernel restriction explains abstractly why return-map determinants and primitive-orbit covolumes occur in trace formulas.
limits: The displayed Selberg formula assumes a restricted hyperbolic setting and test-function conditions, while the flow formula assumes graph-diagonal transversality. The two normalizations and dynamical spaces are not identified, and neither construction supplies a Hamiltonian whose spectrum is the zeta zeros.

title: Area agreement does not fix emission, absorption, or spectral flow
claim: For the same dilation flow, a symplectic change of coordinates preserves phase-space area and the leading semiclassical count, but different cutoff regions change the sign and finite interpretation of the zeta-shaped term: counted emission-like levels, missing absorption lines, or levels shifted out of a finite interval. The remaining linear terms retain the cutoff identification, so coarse area is invariant while quantum phase, boundary, and regulator data are not.
historical_or_program_relation: The later exact inverse-model comparison refines the Berry-Keating versus Connes semiclassical contrast by replacing the binary present/missing language with interval-dependent spectral flow and by exposing regulator-dependent linear terms.
limits: These agreements concern the smooth counting asymptotic only. They establish neither a discrete quantization of the bare dilation Hamiltonian nor the oscillatory zero count, and symplectic equivalence of cutoff areas is not unitary or spectral equivalence of the quantum models.

title: Self-adjoint extension data are stronger than PT eigenvalue pairing
claim: Modified PT symmetry constrains formal eigenvalues to real values or complex-conjugate pairs but supplies neither positivity nor a self-adjoint domain. By contrast, the half-line momentum construction passes to self-adjoint extensions of momentum squared, chooses Neumann or Dirichlet boundary data, and obtains complete cosine or sine bases in which log absolute momentum is defined. The comparison identifies boundary-extension theory, not spectral pairing alone, as the mechanism that legitimizes an operator basis.
historical_or_program_relation: A non-Hermitian Hilbert-Polya proposal uses PT language to motivate spectral reality, whereas the boundary-state construction explicitly resolves a half-line domain ambiguity before imposing its dual spectral condition.
limits: The half-line construction does not prove that its later zeta boundary condition is complete or yields the required spectrum. The difference Hamiltonian's common domain and self-adjointness remain open. PT pairing plus either parity choice does not prove RH.

title: Arithmetic commutants change which spectrum can look universal
claim: Arithmetic quotients carry infinitely many nonlocal Hecke correspondences commuting with the Laplacian, so their Laplace levels have extra organization and the random-matrix comparison is reassigned to Hecke spectra. The non-arithmetic triangle analysis sharpens the obstruction: even exponentially growing orbit-length multiplicity need not spoil GOE behavior when its exponent is below one half, because the diagonal form factor still vanishes within its shrinking validity window.
historical_or_program_relation: Sarnak's operator reassignment explains why arithmetic structure can invalidate a generic Laplace-level universality claim without discarding random-matrix ideas; Bogomolny's exponent calculation then prevents orbit degeneracy alone from being used as a converse diagnostic of arithmetic spectral statistics.
limits: The non-arithmetic multiplicities are finite-range numerical fits and the asymptotic form-factor conclusion is conditional on an assumed multiplicity law and diagonal approximation. Hecke spectra, Laplace spectra, and zeta-zero statistics are distinct objects here; no Hilbert-Polya realization follows.

title: A boundary that reproduces fluctuations may merely encode them
claim: The wiggly-boundary inverse problem reconstructs phase-space boundaries from a prescribed density fluctuation, so agreement with a target spectrum can be achieved by placing the target into boundary geometry. Connes's naturality criterion rejects exactly this answer-encoding move, while the inverse-model perturbation tests show that simple level shifts or prime deletions instead produce smooth arctangent or multi-gamma responses rather than the irregular zero count. Together they distinguish fitting from a mechanism that derives fluctuations.
historical_or_program_relation: The natural Hilbert-Polya program supplies the falsifier, the semiclassical boundary program exhibits how inverse fitting works, and the cyclic-RG inverse model provides bounded negative evidence for two seemingly natural attempts to generate the fluctuations dynamically.
limits: The boundary inversion is only semiclassical and is unique only in its monotone regime. The failed perturbation and deletion routes are not a no-go theorem for all inverse models. This comparison supplies a diagnostic of explanation, not evidence for or against RH.

title: Mellin pole bookkeeping and a dynamical trace formula carry different proof burdens
claim: The Lorentz-gas route sends primitive lattice-horizon sums through a Mellin transform to inverse-zeta factors, so the proposed RH-sensitive remainder depends on closing a contour past the corresponding poles. The trace-formula route instead restricts a flow graph to the diagonal under transversality and derives orbit weights from the return-map determinant. Both begin with dynamics, but only the second cited mechanism establishes a distributional fixed-point identity; the first still lacks the contour estimate that would turn pole bookkeeping into an asymptotic theorem.
historical_or_program_relation: The comparison places a recent transport heuristic beside the established fixed-point architecture it would need to emulate in rigor: a dynamics-to-arithmetic transform is not interchangeable with a proved spectral-orbit trace identity.
limits: The Lorentz-gas source explicitly calls its RH connection formal and does not prove an equivalence even in a simpler related billiard. The abstract flow formula does not validate that contour closure, identify the Lorentz dynamics with zeta dynamics, or produce a zeta operator. No physical transport claim is promoted to a theorem about zeta.

title: Zero factorization transfers rather than solves the operator problem
claim: When flat Fourier diagonalization is lost in curved space, the zeta-field construction replaces an undefined nonlocal completed-zeta operator by a regularized Hadamard product and a formal sum of zero-indexed local second-order fields. The difference-Hamiltonian audit identifies the complementary requirement that a spectral claim needs a common domain, true adjoint, completeness, and self-adjointness. Factorization exposes modes but leaves reconstruction, convergence, covariance, and operator-domain obligations intact.
historical_or_program_relation: The cosmological field program moves from a global nonlocal symbol to local zero-labelled factors, while the Hilbert-Polya program makes explicit why formal factors or eigenfunctions cannot substitute for a closed spectral operator.
limits: The curved-space equivalence is formal and already indexes fields by assumed zero data; it is not an independently derived spectrum. The local mass interpretation is a physical model, not a theorem about zeta or cosmology, and the comparison proves neither self-adjointness nor RH.

title: Group-compatible boundary dynamics do not fix the physical spectrum
claim: In the black-hole dilation proposal, centrality of a D4 element makes a phase-space identification compatible with the finite group action, while commutation with the Hamiltonian propagates that identification along dilation trajectories. Those algebraic checks do not decide whether the resulting lines are emission or absorption, whether the states are complete, or how to resolve an unbounded-below spectrum; the difference-Hamiltonian program shows that these questions ultimately require a controlled domain, adjoint, completeness, and self-adjointness rather than symmetry covariance alone.
historical_or_program_relation: The gauged-CPT proposal attempts to derive a dilation boundary from physical symmetry instead of choosing a cutoff solely for spectral fit; the operator-domain audit supplies the independent mathematical gate that such a symmetry-selected boundary would still have to pass.
limits: Gauged CPT, the phase-space quotient, and its black-hole interpretation are hypotheses of the physical model, not consequences of zeta theory. The cited units do not establish a common operator, a lower-bounded quantum system, a complete microstate account, or RH; spectral coincidence cannot select among those interpretations.
